clues.text: An unpublished collection of these works by Allen Ginsberg begins by describing him drinking sugarless tea.
Poems of this type were published in the collections “Shriveled Chestnuts” and “The Seashell Game”.
The first Westerner known to have engaged in this literary genre is the Dutchman Hendrik Doeff, and R. H. Blyth later popularized it in the English-speaking world.

clues.text: This poetic form includes a “cutting word,” which is often translated as a pause.
Many of these works are collected in the travelogue The Narrow Road to the Deep North, and they were derived from renga.
In poems in this form, the term "kigo" is used to describe seasonal references.
Examples of these types of poems often focus on ( *) nature and the seasons, and an often-cited one describes a frog jumping into a pond.
The sound of water as a frog jumped into a pond inspired Matsuo Basho to write what style of Japanese poetry, which in English consists of three lines of five, seven, and five syllables.
Matsuo Basho authored many of what type of seventeen-syllable poems, common in Japan?
Name this Japanese form of poetry that follows a 5-7-5 syllable scheme.

clues.text: The narrator of this novel is amazed when one group does not attack their employers despite having only rotten hippo meat to eat.
In this novel, a Russian assistant to the protagonist is called “Harlequin” because of his multicolored clothing.
The narrator of this work alludes to the Book of Matthew when he describes a city as a “whited sepulchre.”
This book’s narrator feels nature’s “invading…vengeful rush” before talking to a character’s mistress.
The narrator of this novel is assisted by a Russian named “Harlequin” at the Inner Station.

Narrating from aboard the Nellie, the protagonist suffers from a lack of rivets for his ship prior to meeting a Russian traveler that admires a character who decorates the Inner Station with human heads and whose last words are “The Horror!”.
A boat anchored on the Thames River serves as the setting for this work, and that boat is named Nellie.
The central character of this work scrawls “exterminate all the brutes!” in a book, lives in a hut surrounded by shrunken heads, and cries “the horror, the horror!” before dying.
The horror!” on a steamer on the Congo river.
Charles Marlow is sent to meet Kurtz in what novel by Joseph Conrad?
This author claimed that "This sleep of forgetfulness will not last forever" in the conclusion to a long work that includes the death of Magone and the suicide of Sophonisba.
This man wrote "Virtue will take up arms against savagery" in a poem addressed to his country, which ends "Peace, peace, peace!"
This poet portrayed Death being conquered by Fame in the collection Triumphs.
This author compared an old man preparing to see the Veronica icon on pilgrimage to himself, and wrote another poem as a list of contradictory feelings such as “I burn and yet I freeze.”
A “Prayer to the Virgin” ends a collection by this author in which he is “captured” by “lovely eyes” on a day when the “sun’s ray / was darkened.”
He was crowned as the first modern poet laureate on the strength of his epic about the Punic War, Africa.
Scipio Africanus’s victory was detailed in this poet’s epic Africa.

This author of the Rime Sparse (“REE-mey SPAR-sey”), also called the Canzoniere, names a poetic form devised earlier than the Spenserian and Shakespearean forms, in which an eight-line octave precedes a six-line sestet.
This poet’s collection Il Canzoniere contains many examples of the fourteen-line sonnet form named after him.
Name this Italian poet, who wrote about his love for Laura in his namesake sonnet form.
